s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, cutaneous vascular lesions with erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
salient_findings: Multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
Firm, nonscaly, purple erythematous patches and plaques with irregular borders
Thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels dispersed between thickened collagen bundles
key_facts: Female patient in her late 20s
2-year history of skin lesions
Lesions located on left upper arm, left axilla, and lateral thoracic region
No triggers such as local infection, insect bite, or trauma occurred before lesion appearance
No fever, weight loss, or fatigue
Histopathological examination showed irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels
Endothelial cells were plump but displayed no significant cytologic atypia
Immunohistochemistry results positive for CD31, CD34, Ki-67 (<1%)
Immunohistochemistry results negative for podoplanin (D2-40), human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8)

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination showed irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels, and immunohistochemistry results were positive for CD31 and CD34, which are consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma

shortlist.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, and histopathological examination showed irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels, which are similar to Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma

shortlist.label: Tufted angioma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination showed irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels, and clinical presentation of slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, which are consistent with Tufted angioma

shortlist.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, and histopathological examination showed irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels, which are similar to Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma

shortlist.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination showed irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels, and clinical presentation of slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, which are consistent with Retiform hemangioendothelioma

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques with irregular borders, combined with the histopathological findings of thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels and plump endothelial cells, is consistent with retiform hemangioendothelioma. The immunohistochemistry results, including positivity for CD31 and CD34, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: Negative for HHV-8 and lack of systemic symptoms

rejected.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: Lack of Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon and distinct histological features

rejected.label: Tufted angioma
rejected.why: Histological features do not match, including the presence of cannonball-like tufts of capillaries

rejected.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic targetoid appearance and hemosiderin deposition
